suggested_experiment_name: X-ray and gamma-ray limits on ALP lifetime (NuSTAR/XMM-Newton/INTEGRAL)
notes: This is a theoretical/phenomenological reinterpretation paper, NOT a new experimental measurement. It argues that keV-MeV ALPs coupled to electrons decay radiatively (a->gamma-gamma via electron loop), making them unstable on cosmological scales and excluded by X-ray/gamma-ray astronomy (NuSTAR, XMM-Newton, INTEGRAL), thereby invalidating direct-detection DM limits (GERDA, EDELWEISS-III, SuperCDMS, Majorana). No numerical table or explicit X-ray exclusion values are provided; the main result is Fig. 2 (not machine-readable). The data_points I emit are the cosmological lifetime-boundary curve computed from Eq. (5) (g_ae = 1.095e-6*(100 keV/m_a)^3.5), which bounds the dark-grey 'unstable' region — this is the only quantitatively specified curve. The actual X-ray/gamma-ray exclusion (stronger, light-grey region) is not numerically tabulated. Coupling type is unambiguously the ALP-electron coupling g_ae. Confidence low because this is a recast, not a primary limit, and values are derived rather than directly reported. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 2 of Ferreira, Marsh & Muller (arXiv:2202.08858). Plot shows |g_ae| vs m_a (MeV). The lowest exclusion boundary is the light-grey 'X-ray and gamma-ray limits on lifetime' region, which reaches the lowest coupling values at each mass. This boundary follows a power law of roughly slope -3 on log-log (consistent with constant X-ray signal g_ae^2 m_a^6 = const), flattening near the direct-detection floor (~1e-13) at low mass. Above this, direct-detection experiments (LUX, XENON1T, PandaX, XMASS, SuperCDMS, EDELWEISS-III, GERDA, Majorana) and the dark-grey 'Lifetime < 13.8 Gyr' region provide weaker (higher-coupling) constraints.
